I am a PhD candidate in **Organizations and Markets** (Applied Economics) at the Federal University of Pelotas (UFPel), Brazil, where I work on **energy economics** under the supervision of Daniel de Abreu Pereira Uhr. My dissertation is a collection of essays in energy economics, and my broader research interests include **law and economics**, **jurimetrics**, and the economics of public policy.

My background is interdisciplinary: I hold degrees in Law (UFPel), Chemical Engineering (FURG), and Portuguese–Japanese Language and Literature (UNIFRAN), and a Master's in Organizations and Markets (UFPel), with a thesis on the effects of harsher criminal laws — the case of the Maria da Penha Law in Brazil.

Alongside my research, I work as an administrative officer at UFPel, teach Japanese at Centro de Idiomas MAB, and work in localization for Crunchyroll and MX International.

## Interests

- Energy economics and energy law
- Law and economics · jurimetrics
- Applied microeconometrics and public policy evaluation
- Language education and translation/localization studies

## Education

- **PhD in Organizations and Markets** (in progress, 2023–) — UFPel
- **MSc in Organizations and Markets** (2017) — UFPel
- **BA in Portuguese and Japanese** (2023) — UNIFRAN
- **LLB in Law** (2013) — UFPel
- **BSc in Chemical Engineering** (2013) — FURG
